summary: Melanoma architecture rules for epidermal/junctional, dermal, metastatic, ulcerated, regressed, necrotic, and vascular contexts.

rules.claim: Do not consume, split, detach, or notch epidermis during a generic tumor/stroma burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: A dedicated epidermal invasion or ulceration primitive with full-thickness and reactive-change rules.
counterexamples: Expanding a dermal tumor by cutting a remote strip from intact epidermis.
Smoothing the mask by deleting a thin epidermal projection.
expected_morphology: Epidermal continuity and thickness pattern remain unchanged outside an explicit epidermal task.
forbidden_morphology: Epidermal gap, split, isolated remnant, abrupt notch, or remote consumption.
known_limitations: Adnexal epithelium may be merged with epidermis or absent from a coarse profile.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: A junctional-component edit must remain related to the dermoepidermal junction and must not be treated as a free dermal tumor island.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: A profile may label only aggregate tumor; if the junctional component is not reliably visible, avoid structure-specific edits.
counterexamples: Moving a junctional tumor region away from the epidermis.
Creating a detached epidermal-surface tumor island from a dermal anchor.
expected_morphology: The edited component retains an anatomically plausible relationship with the junction.
forbidden_morphology: Detached junctional island, cross-epidermal jump, or bulk filling of normal epidermis.
known_limitations: Pagetoid single cells may be below tissue-mask resolution.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Use broad-boundary deformation for cohesive nests/sheets, but do not turn scattered or discohesive melanoma cells into a solid filled mass.
rules.required_observation: Classify the local component as cohesive nest/sheet versus dispersed single-cell infiltration and select same-pattern references.
exceptions: Mixed growth requires candidate restriction to a single locally coherent pattern.
counterexamples: Applying a convex hull to scattered dermal melanoma cells.
Carving a deep narrow notch into a large cohesive nest.
expected_morphology: Cohesive tumor retains a continuous natural boundary; discohesive tumor retains intervening stromal spacing.
forbidden_morphology: Forced solidification, remote islands, deep angular bites, or invented single-cell spread.
known_limitations: Some metastatic melanomas form sharply circumscribed nodules unlike primary dermal invasion.

rules.claim: Do not infer, create, or repair ulceration from an epidermal/background gap alone; ulceration is a histopathologic finding requiring full-thickness epidermal absence over tumor with associated surface/reactive context.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: A dedicated ulceration primitive reviewed against CAP definitions.
counterexamples: Deleting epidermis to expand tumor and thereby creating false ulceration.
Filling a true ulcerated surface because it resembles background.
expected_morphology: Surface and epidermal geometry remain unchanged in generic burden edits.
forbidden_morphology: Artificial full-thickness defect, false repair, or background-based ulceration inference.
known_limitations: Reliable ulceration assessment may require slide-level context beyond a patch.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Do not equate regression-associated fibrosis/inflammation/melanophages with ordinary stroma or use it as a generic source for tumor growth/regression.
rules.required_observation: Look for fibrosis, inflammatory infiltrate, pigment-laden macrophages, vascular change, attenuated/absent tumor, and epidermal change in context.
exceptions: A dedicated regression primitive with reviewed criteria and an annotation profile capable of representing it.
counterexamples: Expanding tumor uniformly through a regression bed.
Converting regression-associated inflammation to plain stroma.
expected_morphology: Regression-associated structures remain unchanged in a burden-only edit.
forbidden_morphology: Generic stroma substitution, bulk tumor refill, or melanophage-based tumor seeding.
known_limitations: Histologic regression criteria and reporting practices require expert review and may be heterogeneous.

rules.claim: A generic burden edit must not fill a necrotic component, absorb a vessel, or create/remove perivascular or intravascular relationships.
rules.required_observation: Counterfactual histology may be inspected only after generation in reader-only QA; this fact is unavailable to execution selection or veto.
exceptions: Dedicated necrosis or perivascular/intravascular primitives with separate contracts.
counterexamples: Smoothing tumor by filling central necrosis.
Expanding tumor across a small vessel because it is below the morphology kernel size.
expected_morphology: Necrosis and vessel topology remain unchanged outside an explicit primitive.
forbidden_morphology: Necrotic-hole filling, vessel deletion, lumen crossing, or false vascular invasion.
known_limitations: Small vessels may need nuclei/cell annotations or higher magnification for confirmation.
Reader-only pathology facts are excluded from the execution knowledge bundle.

rules.claim: Choose references and interface priors from the same primary/metastatic and source-site context; do not assume epidermal or dermal architecture at metastatic sites.
rules.required_observation: Require primary/metastatic status, source site, presence of epidermis, and local tumor growth pattern before planning.
exceptions: A reviewed hierarchical fallback may be used with explicit uncertainty if no matched references exist.
counterexamples: Applying a dermoepidermal invasion pattern to a lymph-node metastasis.
Using metastatic nodule compactness thresholds for a junctional primary lesion.
expected_morphology: Interface reasoning matches the anatomical tissue actually present in the patch.
forbidden_morphology: Epidermis-dependent planning without epidermis or cross-site morphology transfer without qualification.
known_limitations: CaseContext presently carries this stratum in annotation-profile provenance rather than a dedicated field.
